mapping.caption: Mapping rules
mapping.empty: No rules yet. Add a rule to give members of a group access in Pagehall.
mapping.groupHint: Searches the groups of {provider} as you type. Groups are matched by their ID.
mapping.groupPlaceholder: Name or ID of the group
mapping.noGroups: No group found. Type the ID of the group to use it.
mapping.useAsId: Use this text as group ID
mapping.accounts: {count, plural, one {# account in Pagehall} other {# accounts in Pagehall}}
mapping.synchronizedGroup: Also add the members to a synchronized group in Pagehall
mapping.synchronizedGroupHint: The group is created with the name of the provider group and can only be changed in the provider.
mapping.makeHome: Make this organization the home organization
mapping.makeHomeHint: Only needed when rules lead into several organizations. Otherwise the first organization an account joins becomes its home organization. When several rules name a home organization, the first rule in the list decides.
mapping.instanceRoleNote: Instance roles never grant access to the content of organizations. Groups of organizations in Pagehall can never receive them.
mapping.previewOrganization: {count, plural, one {# person becomes a member of {organization}.} other {# people become members of {organization}.}}
mapping.previewInstance: {count, plural, one {# person receives the instance role {role}.} other {# people receive the instance role {role}.}}
mapping.previewAccounts: {count, plural, one {# of them has an account already.} other {# of them have an account already.}}
mapping.previewSplit: {accounts} of them have an account already, {later} get one at their next sign-in.
mapping.removeDescription: Members of {name} lose what this rule granted at their next sign-in or sync. Access granted by hand stays.
mapping.hint: Rules apply at every sign-in and sync. Removing someone from the group in {provider} removes what the rule granted. Groups created by rules are read-only in Pagehall.
mapping.byNameTitle: Groups are identified by their names
mapping.byName: {provider} sends group names, not identifiers. Renaming a group in {provider} breaks every rule for it until the rule is changed here.

sync.started: Synchronization started. Results appear here in about a minute.

signInOnly.generic: Profile and groups of this provider update at every sign-in. It has no directory Pagehall could synchronize with in the background; with a SCIM connection, the provider sends changes at once.
signInOnly.google: Google Workspace is only used to sign in. Turn on group synchronization in the settings to read groups and synchronize them in the background.
signInOnly.entraId: This provider is only read at sign-in.
signInOnly.saml: Profile and groups of this provider update at every sign-in. SAML has no directory Pagehall could synchronize with in the background.
signInOnly.ldap: This directory is only read at sign-in.

sync.caption: Synchronization runs
sync.cancelledSummary: Stopped on request. Changes made until then stay.
sync.cancelRequested: The run stops before the next account.
sync.failedWithoutReason: The run failed without a reason. Check the connection and try again.
sync.intervalHint: Groups and account status are also updated at every sign-in.
sync.whenDisabledHint: Accounts disabled or deleted in {provider} are deactivated in Pagehall and reactivated when enabled again. Pagehall never deletes accounts.
sync.groupSyncHint: Without it, Google Workspace is only used to sign in, and mapping rules see no groups.
sync.adminRoleSetup: In the Google Admin console, assign the prebuilt role Groups Reader to the service account under Account > Admin roles. Pagehall then reads groups as the service account itself, without acting for a person.
sync.delegationWarning: With domain-wide delegation the service account acts as the administrator below and may use everything its scopes allow for the whole domain. Prefer the administrator role unless your setup requires delegation.
sync.readUsersHint: Needs a role that can also read users, for example a custom role with Users > Read. Without it, Pagehall does not see suspensions: a suspended person can no longer sign in through Google, but open sessions run until they expire.
sync.adminEmailHint: The service account acts on behalf of this administrator through domain-wide delegation.
sync.keyPlaceholder: Paste the JSON key of the service account

identityProviders.title: Sign-in methods
identityProviders.description: How people sign in to this instance. Organizations follow from group mapping after sign-in.
identityProviders.removeDescription: Removes the provider, its rules and all identities linked through it. To stop sign-ins for a while, deactivate it instead.
identityProviders.removeConfirm: This cannot be undone. Accounts and their content stay.

removal.accountsWithoutSignIn: {count, plural, one {# account has no other way to sign in and cannot sign in any more.} other {# accounts have no other way to sign in and cannot sign in any more.}}
removal.accounts: {count, plural, =0 {No account is linked to this provider.} one {# account loses its identity of this provider.} other {# accounts lose their identity of this provider.}}
removal.grants: {count, plural, =0 {No membership or role granted by its rules is withdrawn.} one {# membership or role granted by its rules is withdrawn.} other {# memberships and roles granted by its rules are withdrawn.}}
removal.rules: {count, plural, =0 {There are no mapping rules.} one {# mapping rule is removed.} other {# mapping rules are removed.}}
removal.groups: {count, plural, =0 {There are no synchronized groups.} one {# synchronized group becomes an ordinary group and keeps its members and permissions.} other {# synchronized groups become ordinary groups and keep their members and permissions.}}

secondFactor.title: Second factor
secondFactor.mode: Second factor after a sign-in through this provider

modes.pagehall: Always ask for a Pagehall second factor

hints.provider: A sign-in through this provider is complete. Set up multi-factor authentication in the provider.
hints.providerProof: The provider must report multi-factor authentication in its sign-in token. Without it, Pagehall asks for its own second factor; people without one set one up first.
hints.pagehall: After every sign-in through this provider, Pagehall asks for its own second factor; people without one set one up first.

secondFactor.proofValuesHint: Values of the amr claim that count as multi-factor authentication, separated by commas. Most providers send mfa.
secondFactor.proofValuesInvalid: Enter 1 to 20 values of up to 50 characters, separated by commas.

directoryModes.pagehall: Always ask for a Pagehall second factor

directoryHints.pagehall: A directory password proves no second factor. After every sign-in with it, Pagehall asks for its own second factor; people without one set one up first.
directoryHints.provider: A directory password proves no second factor. Pagehall still asks for one where the instance or an organization requires it.

status.title: Status
status.deactivatedNotice: Nobody can sign in through it and it is not synchronized. Its settings, rules and groups stay. Activate it again in the settings.
status.deactivateDescription: Stops sign-ins and synchronization through this provider. Everything else stays, and you can activate it again at any time.
status.deactivateConfirm: Nobody can sign in through this provider any more, and the sessions that came from it end now. Settings, rules, groups and access stay.
status.activateDescription: People can sign in through this provider again, and synchronization continues.

identityProviders.emptyDescription: Add Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or another OIDC provider, so people sign in with their work account.
identityProviders.domainHint: The sign-in page chooses the provider by the domain of the e-mail address or sign-in name people enter.
identityProviders.noPermission: Your roles do not allow you to change identity providers.

warnings.expiringAction: Create a new credential at the provider and add it here before then, or sign-in through this provider stops working.
warnings.stoppedAction: Add a valid credential from the provider, then test the sign-in.
warnings.metadataTitle: The metadata of {name} could not be refreshed
warnings.metadataRefreshFailed: Metadata of {name} could not be refreshed at {time}: {error}. Pagehall keeps using the last good metadata. Check the metadata address or upload the file again.
warnings.caExpiring: The CA certificate of {name} expires on {date}
warnings.caExpiringAction: Upload the new CA certificate of the directory in the provider's connection settings before then, or Pagehall can no longer connect to the directory.
warnings.noGraphTitle: {name} cannot read groups through Microsoft Graph
warnings.noGraph: Entra ID leaves out the groups of people in more than 150 groups. Without access to Microsoft Graph, these accounts lose their groups and the access the rules give. Add the client ID of an app registration and its credential.

overview.rulesHint: Groups that grant access in Pagehall.
overview.missingGroups: {count, plural, one {# rule points to a group that no longer exists} other {# rules point to groups that no longer exist}}

identityProviders.redirectUriHint: Enter this address in the app registration of your provider.

fields.name: Name on the sign-in page
fields.nameHint: For example Microsoft or the name of your company.
fields.tenantIdHint: Found in the overview of your Entra ID tenant.
fields.tenantIdInvalid: Enter the tenant ID as shown in Entra ID, for example 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c21-5d6f0a8b2e17.
fields.issuerHint: The address of the provider. Pagehall reads its configuration from /.well-known/openid-configuration.
fields.googleDomains: Enter at least one Google Workspace domain.
fields.algorithmHint: The only algorithm Pagehall accepts for ID tokens from this provider.

attributes.description: Pagehall recognizes an account by the provider's identifier, never by its e-mail address. The other attributes fill the profile and update at every sign-in.
attributes.identifierHint: Never changes, also when names or addresses change.
attributes.fixed: Fixed for this type of provider
attributes.emailHint: Used for notifications, invitations and the home organization by domain.
attributes.signInNameHint: Shown next to the e-mail address, so people recognize their work account.
attributes.googleFixed: Google Workspace sends the e-mail address, name and user ID; there is nothing to choose.

claims.groupsHint: Leave empty if the provider does not send groups.
claims.groupNamesHint: Optional. Groups are matched by their ID; names are only shown.

saml.identifierHint: An attribute that never changes for a person, such as objectGUID.
saml.identifierHintGeneric: Leave empty to use the persistent NameID of the identity provider.
saml.optionalHint: Optional. Leave empty if the identity provider does not send it.

groupValuesHint.adfs: In the claim rules of the relying party trust, send Token-Groups as SIDs. SIDs stay the same when a group is renamed.
groupValuesHint.generic: What the groups attribute contains. Identifiers stay the same when a group is renamed.

saml.namesWarning: With group names, renaming a group in the provider breaks the rules for it. Use identifiers if the provider can send them.

accounts.createHint: Without this, only invited people and existing accounts can sign in.
accounts.domainsHint: Enter every domain that is verified in the tenant, for sign-in names and for e-mail addresses, for example example.com and example.at. The sign-in page sends people with these domains to this provider, e-mail addresses in them count as confirmed, and accounts are created only for them. A domain belongs to one provider only.
accounts.domainsHintGoogle: Enter every domain of your Google Workspace, for sign-in names and for e-mail addresses. The sign-in page sends people with these domains to Google.
accounts.domainsInvalid: Enter domains like example.org, separated by commas.
accounts.requireGroupHint: Usually not needed: restrict access in the provider instead. Use this only when the provider cannot restrict access itself.
accounts.groupsHint: IDs of the groups at the provider, separated by commas. Membership in one of them is enough.
accounts.linkHint: When an account with the same verified address exists, the person confirms once with its password and second factor. Pagehall never links accounts automatically.
accounts.domainsHintDirectory: Enter the domains of the e-mail addresses and sign-in names in the directory, for example example.com. The sign-in page asks people with these domains for their directory password, and accounts are created only for them. A domain belongs to one provider only.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.expiresOnHint: Pagehall reminds you 30 and 7 days before.
credentials.certificateHint: Pagehall creates a key pair. Upload the certificate to the app registration; the private key never leaves Pagehall.
credentials.certificateUpload: Download the certificate and upload it to the app registration at your provider.
credentials.removeDescription: Pagehall stops using it at once. Make sure a newer credential works first.
credentials.bindPasswordHint: Pagehall stores it encrypted and uses it only to search the directory.
credentials.signingHint: Pagehall creates a new key pair for signing its requests. Its metadata lists the new certificate at once.
credentials.signingUpload: Pagehall's metadata contains the new certificate. Let the identity provider load the metadata again, or download the certificate and add it there. Remove the old certificate once the identity provider uses the new one.

addDescriptions.oidc: The current credential keeps working until you remove it, so you can switch without interruption.
addDescriptions.saml: The current certificate keeps working until you remove it, so the identity provider can switch without interruption.
addDescriptions.ldap: Change the password of the service account in the directory first, then enter it here. Remove the old one afterwards.

noneDescriptions.oidc: Sign-in through this provider does not work until you add a client secret or a certificate.
noneDescriptions.saml: Pagehall cannot sign its requests until you add a signing certificate.
noneDescriptions.ldap: Pagehall cannot search the directory until you enter the password of the service account.

renewHints.oidc: During a renewal, old and new credential both work. Remove the old one once the new one is in place.
renewHints.saml: During a renewal, Pagehall's metadata lists old and new certificate. Remove the old one once the identity provider uses the new one.
renewHints.ldap: The password has no expiry date in Pagehall. To rotate it, enter the new password and remove the old one.

logo.label: Logo
logo.hint: Shown on the sign-in button. PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 256 KiB. Microsoft and Google use their own buttons.
logo.removeDescription: The sign-in button shows a key icon instead.

test.title: Test the connection
test.description: Sign in once with a test account. Nothing is saved, and no account is created.
test.summary: Received {claims, plural, one {# claim} other {# claims}} and {groups, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}}.
test.failedAction: Check the client ID, the credential and the redirect URI at your provider, then test again.
test.unverifiedTitle: The e-mail address is not in the provider's domains
test.unverified: {email} is not in one of the configured domains. Pagehall does not link or create accounts for it.
test.subject: Identifier
test.noClaims: The provider sent no claims or attributes.
test.claimsHint: Tokens, hashes and secrets are never shown.

wizard.title: Add identity provider

connectionHints.entraId: In the Entra admin center, create an app registration. After saving, Pagehall shows the redirect URI to enter there. Under Enterprise applications, turn on Assignment required and assign the groups that may use Pagehall.
connectionHints.google: In the Google Cloud console, create an OAuth client of type Web application. After saving, Pagehall shows the redirect URI to enter there.
connectionHints.generic: Create a confidential OIDC client at your provider. After saving, Pagehall shows the redirect URI to enter there.

entraId.title: Microsoft Entra ID
entraId.hint: OIDC with groups through Microsoft Graph.
entraId.capabilities: Groups and account status are synchronized in the background; disabled accounts are deactivated.

google.title: Google Workspace
google.hint: OIDC with groups through the Directory API.
google.capabilities: Sign-in only at first. Group synchronization can be turned on later with a service account.

oidc.title: Other OIDC provider
oidc.hint: Keycloak, Authentik, Okta, Zitadel and others.
oidc.capabilities: Profile and groups update at every sign-in. There is no background synchronization.

saml.title: SAML 2.0
saml.hint: ADFS, Shibboleth or Entra ID through SAML.
saml.capabilities: Profile and groups update at every sign-in. With Entra ID, groups can also be synchronized through Microsoft Graph.

ldap.title: LDAP or Active Directory
ldap.hint: Sign-in with directory passwords and group sync.
ldap.capabilities: Groups and account status are synchronized in the background; disabled accounts are deactivated.

savedHints.oidc: Enter this redirect URI in the app registration at your provider, then continue.
savedHints.saml: Enter these values at the identity provider, or let it read Pagehall's metadata, then continue.
savedHints.ldap: Pagehall reaches the directory with the service account. Choose below how people sign in.

samlHints.entraId: In the Entra admin center, create an enterprise application with SAML single sign-on. After saving, Pagehall shows its entity ID and reply URL to enter there.
samlHints.adfs: In ADFS, add a relying party trust. After saving, Pagehall shows its metadata address, which ADFS can read.
samlHints.generic: Create a SAML service provider at your identity provider. After saving, Pagehall shows its entity ID, its assertion consumer service URL and its metadata.

metadataUrlHints.entraId: The App Federation Metadata URL from the SAML settings of the enterprise application.
metadataUrlHints.generic: The address of the identity provider's metadata, starting with https://.

wizard.metadataFileHint: The XML file with the metadata of the identity provider. Without an address, upload a new file whenever its certificate changes.
wizard.metadataFileRequired: Choose the metadata file of the identity provider.
wizard.fileUnreadable: The file could not be read. Choose it again or try another file.

ldapHints.activeDirectory: Create a service account in Active Directory that may read people and groups. It needs no other rights.
ldapHints.generic: Create a service account in the directory that may read people and groups, for example in OpenLDAP or FreeIPA. It needs no other rights.

wizard.caHint: Optional. Only needed when the server certificate was issued by your own certificate authority.
wizard.caFailedTitle: The provider is saved, but the CA certificate is not
wizard.caFailedAction: Continue and upload the right CA certificate in the test step or in the connection settings.
wizard.graphHint: SAML assertions from Entra ID carry at most 150 groups. With an app registration that has the application permissions GroupMember.Read.All and User.Read.All, Pagehall loads the rest through Microsoft Graph and also synchronizes accounts in the background. You can skip this step and add it later in the settings.

saml.entityIdHint: Also called identifier or audience at the identity provider.
saml.acsUrlHint: Also called reply URL. The identity provider sends the sign-in response to this address.
saml.metadataUrlHint: Most identity providers can read this address or the downloaded file, so you do not have to enter the values above by hand.
saml.noMetadataUrl: Pagehall could not load the metadata yet, so nobody can sign in. Check the metadata address and load it again.
saml.noMetadataFile: Upload the metadata file of the identity provider. Nobody can sign in until then.
saml.refreshFailedTitle: The metadata could not be refreshed
saml.sourceHint: With an address, Pagehall loads the metadata again every day and picks up new certificates of the identity provider by itself.
saml.metadataAddressHint: The address of the identity provider's metadata, starting with https://.
saml.idpEntityId: Entity ID of the identity provider
saml.certificatesHint: Pagehall accepts only responses signed with one of these certificates.
saml.idpInitiated: Allow sign-in started at the identity provider
saml.idpInitiatedHint: Sign-in started at the identity provider cannot be tied to a request from this browser, so an attacker could sign someone into the attacker's account. Turn it on only if people must start from a portal such as the Microsoft app launcher.
saml.requireSignedResponseHint: The assertion must always be signed. Entra ID and ADFS sign only the assertion by default; turn this on only if your identity provider also signs the whole response.
saml.encryptedAssertionsHint: The identity provider encrypts the assertion with Pagehall's certificate from the metadata. Turn it on only after the identity provider is set up for it, or sign-in stops working.
saml.graphClientIdHint: Optional. With an app registration and a credential for it, Pagehall reads groups beyond the token limit and synchronizes the directory through Microsoft Graph.

ldap.urlHint: For example ldaps://dc01.example.org. Use ldaps:// or ldap:// with StartTLS, so passwords are never sent unencrypted.
ldap.urlInvalid: Enter an address such as ldaps://dc01.example.org, without a path.
ldap.urlInvalidStartTls: Enter an ldap:// address while StartTLS is on. To use ldaps://, turn StartTLS off first.
ldap.startTlsHint: Encrypts the ldap:// connection before any password is sent.
ldap.startTlsLdaps: Only for ldap:// addresses; ldaps:// is encrypted already.
ldap.plainWarning: Without StartTLS, passwords travel unencrypted. Pagehall refuses such a connection unless the instance runs with insecure identity providers allowed.
ldap.bindDnHint: The distinguished name of the account Pagehall uses to search the directory, for example CN=pagehall,OU=Service,DC=example,DC=org.
ldap.userBaseDnHint: Pagehall searches for people below this entry, for example OU=Staff,DC=example,DC=org.
ldap.groupBaseDnHint: Pagehall searches for groups below this entry, for example OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=org.
ldap.dnInvalid: Enter a distinguished name such as OU=Staff,DC=example,DC=org.
ldap.userFilterHint: Only entries matching this LDAP filter can sign in.
ldap.groupFilterHint: Only entries matching this LDAP filter count as groups.
ldap.filterInvalid: Enter an LDAP filter in parentheses, such as (objectClass=person).
ldap.signInAttributeHint: What people enter on the sign-in page besides their password.
ldap.attributeInvalid: Enter an LDAP attribute name such as mail.
ldap.groupMembershipHint: Where the directory records who belongs to a group.
ldap.disabledAttributeHint: Optional. Leave empty if the directory does not mark disabled accounts.
ldap.disabledValuesHint: Separated by commas. Without values, any value of the attribute means disabled.
ldap.disabledValuesInvalid: Enter up to 20 values of up to 256 characters, separated by commas.
ldap.caDescription: Needed when the server certificate of the directory was issued by your own certificate authority.
ldap.caNoneHint: Pagehall trusts only certificates of public certificate authorities.
ldap.caRemoveDescription: Pagehall then trusts only public certificate authorities. If the directory uses a certificate of your own authority, sign-in and sync stop working.

directoryTest.title: Test the directory
directoryTest.description: Pagehall connects with the service account and searches for a person. Nothing is saved, and no account is created.
directoryTest.signInName: Sign-in name of a test person
directoryTest.signInNameHint: Optional. Without it, Pagehall shows the first person it finds.
directoryTest.workedDescription: Pagehall reached the server, trusted its certificate, signed in with the service account and found a person.

actions.connection: Check the server address, the port and the firewall between Pagehall and the directory, then test again.
actions.certificate: Upload the CA certificate that issued the server's certificate, then test again.
actions.serviceAccount: Check the DN and the password of the service account, then test again.
actions.search: Check the base DNs and the filters, then test again.

scim.intro: With SCIM, the provider sends changes of people and groups to Pagehall at once instead of waiting for the next sign-in or synchronization. Accounts are created before the first sign-in and deactivated, never deleted.
scim.accounts: Everyone assigned to the app at the provider gets an account, even when account creation at first sign-in is off.
scim.entraSetup: Entra ID needs P1 or higher. In the enterprise application, open Provisioning, choose Automatic, enter the URL below as tenant URL and the token as secret token. In the attribute mappings for users, map objectId to externalId.
scim.genericSetup: Enter the URL below and the token as bearer token at your provider. externalId must carry the identifier the provider uses at sign-in.
scim.urlHint: The SCIM endpoint of this provider.
scim.noTokens: No token yet. SCIM is off until you create one.
scim.lastRequestDetail: {time} · in the last 24 hours {changes, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}} accepted, {failed, plural, one {# request} other {# requests}} refused
scim.noRequests: No request yet. Test the connection at the provider.
scim.leads: While SCIM is on, it leads: the background synchronization of this provider runs once a day as a reconciliation. The sync log shows SCIM requests with their changes and errors.
scim.onlyOnce: Copy the token now and enter it at the provider. Pagehall shows it only this once.
scim.overlap: The previous token keeps working for seven days, so the provider is not interrupted while you change it.
scim.removeDescription: Requests with this token are refused at once.
scim.removeLast: Requests with this token are refused at once. Without a token, SCIM is off and the background synchronization returns to its interval.

identities.title: Linked sign-ins
identities.unlinkDescription: The person can no longer sign in with this identity. Their account, content and memberships stay.
identities.none: No sign-ins through providers are linked.
identities.noneOwn: You do not sign in through an identity provider.
identities.ownHint: Your administrator links sign-ins through providers. You can unlink one while another way to sign in remains.
identities.unlinkOwnDescription: You can no longer sign in with this identity, and the sessions that came from it end. Your account, content and memberships stay.
identities.linkDescription: Connect a sign-in at a provider to this account, for example after a change of the e-mail address.
identities.subject: Identifier at the provider
identities.subjectHint: The stable ID of the person at the provider, for example the object ID in Entra ID. A test sign-in shows it.

common.copyFailed: Copying failed because the browser blocked access to the clipboard. Select the text and copy it manually.

emergencyRecipients.title: Emergency sign-in
emergencyRecipients.description: When you sign in with your password while password sign-in is off, these people are told at once. You, as the instance owner, are always told.
emergencyRecipients.ownerOnly: Only the instance owner can change who is told about an emergency sign-in.
emergencyRecipients.administratorsHint: All instance owners and administrators get a notification.
emergencyRecipients.accountsHint: They get a notification in Pagehall and by e-mail.
emergencyRecipients.addressesHint: Addresses outside Pagehall, for example a security team, separated by commas. Up to 20.
emergencyRecipients.addressesInvalid: Enter up to 20 valid e-mail addresses, separated by commas.

withheldRoles.title: {count, plural, one {One of your administrative roles is paused} other {# of your administrative roles are paused}}
withheldRoles.description: Pagehall could not read your groups from {provider} for a while, so administrative roles that come from those groups are paused for safety. Your memberships stay. The roles return as soon as your groups can be read again, for example at your next sign-in. Your administrators were told.

withoutOrganization.title: No organization is assigned to you yet
withoutOrganization.description: Your account was created, but it is not a member of any organization yet. The administrators of this instance were told and will assign one. You can already change your preferences and security settings.

insecureProviders.title: Identity providers are not checked strictly
insecureProviders.description: PAGEHALL_INSECURE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS is set, so identity providers may use plain HTTP and any host. Use this only for local tests and remove the variable from the server configuration before people sign in.

rail.label: Main navigation
rail.notificationsUnread: Notifications, {count, plural, one {# unread} other {# unread}}

errors.notFoundDescription: The page does not exist, or you do not have access to it. Check the address or go to the start page.
errors.forbiddenDescription: Your roles do not allow you to see this page. Ask an owner of the organization for access if you need it.
errors.failedTitle: This page could not be loaded

validation.tooShort: Use at least {minimum, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}.
validation.tooLong: Use at most {maximum, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}.
validation.range: Enter a whole number from {minimum} to {maximum}.
validation.format: This value has the wrong format.
validation.slug: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
validation.domain: Enter a domain such as example.org.
validation.instanceUrl: Enter an address such as https://wiki.example.org, without a path.

problems.lastSignInMethod: This is the last working way to sign in to the account. Another identity of an active provider, a passkey, or a password while password sign-in is on would keep it reachable. Add one of them first, then unlink again.
problems.lastCredential: This is the provider's only credential. Add a new one before you remove it.
problems.identityInUse: This identity is already linked to another account. Unlink it there first.
problems.passwordSignInDisabled: Password sign-in is turned off for this instance. Sign in through your provider or with a passkey.
problems.invalidProviderConfiguration: Pagehall could not use this provider configuration. Check the issuer, tenant or client ID against your provider's settings and save again.
problems.resetOwnSecondFactor: You cannot reset your own second factor here, because that would bypass it. Sign in with a recovery code or ask another administrator.
problems.endOwnSessions: Your own sessions are not ended from the account list. End them on your Security page.
problems.roleNeedsAccountOrGroup: Roles can only go to individual people and groups, not to everyone at once. Choose people or groups instead.
problems.unknown: The server gave an unexpected answer. Try again; if it keeps failing, ask your administrator to check the server log.
problems.networkError: Pagehall cannot be reached. Check your connection and try again.
problems.invalidInput: Some entries are not valid. Correct the marked fields and try again.
problems.passwordPolicy: The password does not meet the requirements. Choose a longer or less common password.
problems.passwordTooLong: The password is too long. Use at most 256 characters.
problems.passwordCommon: This password is too common. Choose another one.
problems.invalidToken: The link is not valid or has expired. Request a new link.
problems.sameEmail: This is already your e-mail address. Enter a different one.
problems.invalidSmtpConfiguration: The mail server settings are not valid: credentials need a TLS connection. Choose TLS or STARTTLS, or remove the credentials.
problems.invalidSetting: The value is not valid for this setting. Check the allowed range and try again.
problems.invalidPrincipal: This role does not fit their kind of account. Choose another role or person.
problems.roleNotAssignable: This role cannot be assigned here. Choose another role.
problems.ownerExpiry: The owner role cannot expire. Remove the expiry date.
problems.expiryInPast: The date lies in the past. Choose a date in the future.
problems.expiryRequired: An expiry date is required here. Choose one.
problems.expiryTooLate: The expiry date is later than the maximum lifetime allows. Choose an earlier date.
problems.invalidOwner: This account cannot become the owner because it is not an active member. Choose another account.
problems.invalidLogo: The file is not a PNG, JPEG or WebP image of at most 256 KiB. Choose another image.
